subject: Medlytics integration: technical agreement & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Medlytics integration: recap of technical pain, fit notes, and proposed next steps

Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned before the technical workshop: 

Key pain points you mentioned
- Latency spikes on your existing embeddings + rerank flow when under load (esp during morning batch jobs)
- Quality drift on reranker after weekly model retrains — manual tuning is costly
- Need structured outputs (JSON schema) from generative steps for downstream ETL and LH triggers
- Desire to stream longer narrative responses into your UI for progressive rendering (avoid waiting for full response)

What we heard you want
- Stable 95th percentile latency < 350ms for short queries (embedding + rerank path)
- Deterministic fallback behavior if primary model overloads (cheaper 7B variant)
- End-to-end traceability for inference calls for audit and billing

Initial integration/technical fit notes
- SDK: our Python + TypeScript SDKs already support structured output enforcement (schema enforcement + function calling). We recommend using function calling for the ETL-ready payloads and structured outputs for the task-based responses.
- Embeddings/rerank: suggest a hybrid approach — store dense embeddings with periodic re-indexing and surface a small, warm hotset for reranking to reduce cold-cache latency.
- Streaming: our streaming API streams tokens as they’re generated and supports incremental JSON chunks; you’ll want to enable streaming + response delta checksum to reconcile partial parses in the UI.
- Batching & cache: enable per-customer prefix KV caching and a 50–100ms batching window for peak throughput savings.

Compliance & ops
- We noted your SOC2 questionnaire items. Neha will send the SOC2 extracts and suggested audit log retention settings.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical workshop (deep-dive) — Tue Sep 23 at 11:00 PT — confirm? (we can move if your engineers prefer)
2) We’ll share a one-week POC plan: sample dataset, target SLAs, and success metrics (latency, rerank NDCG, cost per 1M tokens)
3) Security checklist items to complete before POC: IP allowlist, KMS integration notes, data retention policy

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (outline + milestone plan)

If that aligns, I’ll lock the workshop and Neha will open the SOC2 packet.

—
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erin Cho <erin.cho@medlytics.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medlytics integration: recap of technical pain, fit notes, and proposed next steps

Thanks Markus — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority order: 1) Embedding + rerank latency stability, 2) structured outputs for our claims ingestion pipeline, 3) streaming for UX.
- For the POC we can provide a sanitized dataset (10k records) and our rerank gold set. We’d like to measure NDCG @10.
- Can you confirm whether function calling will let us validate against a schema server-side and reject malformed outputs with a non-200? That’s important for our downstream pipeline.

Workshop: Sep 23 at 11:00 PT works for our infra lead (Erin) and me. Please send calendar invite.

Also, pricing question: for the POC, do you have a short-term eval pricing or trial credits for compute? That will help us scope running a few aggressive stress tests.

Samir
Director of Product, Medlytics
samir@medlytics.ai | +1 650-555-9987

On Sun, Sep 14, 2025 at 3:02 PM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message quoted above)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Erin Cho <erin.cho@medlytics.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medlytics integration: recap of technical pain, fit notes, and proposed next steps

Samir —

Quick answers inline: 
- Function calling + structured output: yes. Our server will validate against your JSON schema and return a 4xx (structured validation error) if the model output violates the schema when run in strict mode. We can also emit a partial payload and an error field when in permissive mode.
- For the POC pricing: we usually provide evaluation credits for bench tests. I’ve looped in Lauren to propose a trial credit amount and a short pricing anchor for expected POC compute. Lauren — can you propose numbers (cc’d).
- Technical workshop invite: I’m sending a calendar invite for Sep 23 11:00 PT with a short agenda (system architecture, POC milestones, security checklist).

Proposed POC milestones (one-week sprint)
Day 0: onboarding + dataset transfer (we’ll provide an S3 presigned flow)
Day 1–2: baseline measurements (current infra vs Redwood small model)
Day 3–4: integrate streaming + function calling into claims ingestion; run rerank gold set
Day 5: stress test + final metrics + <decision> go/no-go.

Security items Neha will send:
- SOC2 extract (attached): medlytics-soc2-extract.xlsx
- IP allowlist instructions
- KMS integration checklist and our recommended retention (30 days for raw request logs by default)

Attachments: medlytics-soc2-extract.xlsx

Let me know if you want us to stand up a short-lived dedicated pool for the stress window — we can do that but it changes the short-term POC cost.

—
Markus

From: Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Perfect — that all sounds good. We’d like the dedicated pool for the stress window (will accept the trial uplift). Please include expected cost delta in the POC anchor.

Erin and I will prepare the sanitized dataset and the rerank gold set by EOD Sep 19. See you on the 23rd.

—Samir
